name: The Oath-Rings
summary: The deep-folk's identity worn on the body: iron rings bound into the beard, each marking clan, craft, age, oath, grief, war, mastery, or silence. Rings are added at life-milestones and never removed — a living genealogy. When a bearer dies, the rings return to Hallord's Ring-Vault, whose lock opens only to a unanimous clan council. Ten thousand rings hang there, each one a completed life.
origin: Age of Stone — the practice dates to the Deep-Forging's first generation (~410–450 AS)
current_whereabouts: Worn by the living; the Ring-Vault in Hallord holds the dead's.
properties: Each ring type is struck differently: clan rings by the clan, craft rings at the First Forge, silence rings by no visible hand
A bearer's full set reads as biography to anyone fluent in ring-lore
Stealing a dead dwarf's rings is the deepest theft imaginable; wearing them is beyond sacrilege
keepers: Hallord's Door-Keepers guard the vault; the unanimous-council lock has opened eleven times in recorded memory.
value_or_danger: Beyond price to the clans. A forged ring discovered destroys a family's standing for generations.
adventure_hooks: A ring in the vault bears a craft-mark no forge claims — and it was added after its bearer's burial.
Players find a complete ring-set on a body in the Ashlands: the owner walked into the Quiet during the Sundering. Returning them means opening the vault for the twelfth time.
A young dwarf offers players her first oath-ring to hold as collateral; the clan wants to know why.
